import XCTest

/// The cards-media part (scripts/phone-test-plan.ts): its test and the steps only it takes.
extension PhoneJourney {
    /// INF-2125 direction C, the third cards test: pictures, a recording, a thread, a body's choice, out of reach and large type.
    func testCardMediaAndBody() async throws {
        app.launchEnvironment["INFINITARY_TEST_RETRIED_CARD_LAG"] = "3"
        try await launchJoined()
        try await verifyCardMediaAndBody()
    }

    private func verifyCardMediaAndBody() async throws {
        let fixture = try await home("cards-fixture")
        let choice = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["choice"] as? String)
        let chart = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["conversation"] as? String)
        let note = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["note"] as? String)
        // INF-1879: put the staged choice aside without discarding it or answering it.
        showCard(choice)
        let reported = app.staticTexts.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label MATCHES %@", #"[0-9]+ of [0-9]+ answered · 1 changed"#)).firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(reported.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(choice).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertFalse(app.alerts.firstMatch.exists, "Putting a card aside never asks to discard its staged settings")

        showCard(chart)
        // INF-1062: with no bar under it, scrolling a long card leaves the message box where it is, in the column's width.
        if UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone {
            let composer = app.otherElements["phone-composer"].firstMatch
            let before = composer.frame
            app.scrollViews["card-scroll"].swipeUp()
            XCTAssertEqual(composer.frame.minY, before.minY, accuracy: 1, "Scrolling a card does not move the message box")
            XCTAssertEqual(composer.frame.width, before.width, accuracy: 1, "Scrolling a card does not narrow the message box")
            verifyPhoneComposerBounds(app: app)
            try await appearances("card-scrolled", showing: app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
        }
        let pictureElement = app.webViews.images["Blue harbour survey"].firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(pictureElement.waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        reveal(pictureElement); tapOnPhone(pictureElement)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.webViews["card-picture"].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        picture("picture-viewer")
        _ = try await home("capture-picture-start")
        app.webViews["card-picture"].pinch(withScale: 1.6, velocity: 1)
        picture("picture-zoomed")
        _ = try await home("capture-stop")
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["Done"])
        // INF-3107 (the captain's Approve and build): a tapped diagram opens full screen, fitted; a double-tap shows it
        // at its own size where tapped and a second one fits it again; a swipe down while fitted closes it.
        let diagram = app.webViews.images["Harbour approach in three legs"].firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(diagram.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        reveal(diagram); tapOnPhone(diagram)
        let viewer = app.webViews["card-picture"]
        XCTAssertTrue(viewer.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars["Card diagram"].waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        // The viewer's web page reads the drawing out by the diagram's own label.
        XCTAssertTrue(viewer.images["Harbour approach in three legs"].firstMatch.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        // WebKit places the drawing's own frame inside the picture, not where it is drawn, so the zoom is read from
        // the viewer's horizontal scroll bar: one page fitted, more once enlarged.
        let across = viewer.otherElements.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label BEGINSWITH %@", "Horizontal scroll bar")).firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(across.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertEqual(across.label, "Horizontal scroll bar, 1 page", "A diagram opens fitted")
        picture("diagram-viewer")
        viewer.doubleTap()
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in across.label != "Horizontal scroll bar, 1 page" }, object: across, timeout: 10) == .completed,
                      "A double-tap enlarges the diagram: \(across.label)")
        picture("diagram-enlarged")
        viewer.doubleTap()
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in across.label == "Horizontal scroll bar, 1 page" }, object: across, timeout: 10) == .completed,
                      "A second double-tap fits it again: \(across.label)")
        viewer.swipeDown()
        XCTAssertTrue(viewer.waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), "A swipe down while fitted closes the viewer")
        // The home measures the recording and owns its duration label.
        let play = app.webViews.buttons.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label BEGINSWITH %@", "Play the demo,")).firstMatch
        reveal(play)
        _ = try await home("capture-media-start")
        tapOnPhone(play)
        let player = app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "card-recording").firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(player.waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        // The body's Play already starts playback; AVKit may hide its controls before a short clip ends.
        // Completion comes from the real player's end notification, not a transient controls snapshot.
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["recording-finished"].waitForPresence(timeout: 15), app.debugDescription)
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["Play again"])
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["recording-finished"].waitForPresence(timeout: 15))
        let mediaState = XCTAttachment(string: app.debugDescription)
        mediaState.name = "recording-controls"; mediaState.lifetime = .keepAlways; add(mediaState)
        picture("recording-playing")
        _ = try await home("capture-stop")
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["Done"])
        let reply = app.textFields["card-reply"]
        reveal(reply)
        _ = try await home("capture-reply-start")
        focusForPhoneTyping(reply, in: app); reply.typeText("Keep the northern entrance clear.")
        let send = app.buttons["send-reply"]
        reveal(send); tapOnPhone(send)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Keep the northern entrance clear."].waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        // The reply wakes the first mate, whose answer joins this card's thread a turn later. The count is read once that
        // answer is in, or an answer landing after the read leaves the thread one longer than the count.
        let back = app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "card-back").firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(back.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        let answer = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["replyAnswer"] as? String)
        XCTAssertTrue(back.staticTexts[answer].waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        let replied = try await home("card-state", method: "GET")
        let thread = try XCTUnwrap(replied["thread"] as? [String: Any])
        let sent = thread["messages"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? []
        XCTAssertTrue(sent.contains {
            $0["who"] as? String == "captain" && $0["text"] as? String == "Keep the northern entrance clear."
        })
        // INF-1919 (the captain's Approve and build): the send turns the card over to its thread, where the reply shows.
        XCTAssertEqual(app.staticTexts["thread-count"].label, "THREAD · \(sent.count)")
        picture("card-thread-sent")
        // Card turns it back; the face's latest line names the reply, and an answer that lands there lights it.
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["thread-return"])
        let cue = app.buttons["thread-cue"]
        XCTAssertTrue(cue.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertTrue(back.waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), "The face hides the back")
        _ = try await home("thread-answer")
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in cue.value as? String == "1 new" }, object: cue, timeout: 10) == .completed,
                      app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["put-aside-card"].exists, "A landing reply never turns the card")
        picture("card-thread-unread")
        tapOnPhone(cue)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["I kept your harbour reply with this chart."].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        picture("card-thread")
        _ = try await home("capture-stop")
        // Command-backslash turns it back, as on the Mac; the line is read now.
        try await pressPhoneKey("\\", modifiers: .command, in: app)
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in cue.value as? String == "\(sent.count + 1) messages" }, object: cue, timeout: 10) == .completed,
                      app.debugDescription)
        let browser = app.buttons["card-action-browser"]
        reveal(browser); tapOnPhone(browser)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Do this on Test Mac mini."].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))

        _ = try await home("offline")
        outOfReach()
        XCTAssertFalse(app.buttons["put-aside-card"].isEnabled)
        XCTAssertFalse(app.buttons["card-action-body"].isEnabled)
        let atDisconnect = try await home("card-state", method: "GET")
        let bodyButton = app.webViews.buttons["Choose from the body"]
        reveal(bodyButton); tapOnPhone(bodyButton)
        picture("card-out-of-reach")
        _ = try await home("online")
        reach("In reach", timeout: 20)
        let afterReconnect = try await home("card-state", method: "GET")
        let writes: ([String: Any]) -> Int = { state in (state["calls"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? []).filter { $0["channel"] as? String == "inf:cards:act" }.count }
        XCTAssertEqual(writes(afterReconnect), writes(atDisconnect), "An offline body action is never replayed")
        // INF-2553 (the captain: "the card leaves at the tap and the next card is up at once"): the body's choice
        // takes the card off Home while the computer still holds its request, so no second input can reach it.
        _ = try await home("hold-card-action")
        reveal(bodyButton); tapOnPhone(bodyButton)
        _ = try await home("card-action-held")
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(chart).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), "A body choice shows at the tap, before the computer answers")
        picture("card-choice-at-tap")
        _ = try await home("release-card-action")
        XCTAssertFalse(cardHeading(chart).exists, "The computer's answer leaves the choice as shown")
        let bodyChoice = try await home("card-state", method: "GET")
        XCTAssertEqual(writes(bodyChoice), writes(afterReconnect) + 1, "The choice sends one change")
        let bodyPast = try XCTUnwrap(bodyChoice["conversation"] as? [String: Any])
        XCTAssertEqual((bodyPast["ending"] as? [String: Any])?["actionId"] as? String, "body")
        // The choice wakes the first mate; its turn ends before INF-1060 below reads the footer's reply button.
        _ = try await home("script-choice-heard")
        _ = try await home("show-body-past")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Past"].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        XCTAssertEqual((bodyPast["ending"] as? [String: Any])?["by"] as? String, "frame")
        let pastWords = try XCTUnwrap(bodyChoice["conversationEnding"] as? String)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["past-ending"].label.hasPrefix(pastWords), "A script's choice is not credited to the captain")
        // INF-1879: photograph the past card's minus only once its body is drawn, not its incoming shell.
        showCard(chart)
        picture("past-body-choice")
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
        showCard(note)
        // INF-2553 (the captain: "to its place in the stack, with a short notice where you are"): a close the
        // computer refuses brings the card back where it was and says why on Home.
        let refusal = "This card changed on your computer. Look at it again."
        _ = try await home("refuse-next-change", body: #"{"channel":"inf:cards:close","words":"\#(refusal)"}"#)
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
        let notice = app.buttons["change-notice"]
        XCTAssertTrue(notice.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertEqual(notice.label, refusal)
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(note).waitForPresence(timeout: 10), "A refused close puts the card back")
        picture("card-close-refused")
        tapOnPhone(notice)
        XCTAssertTrue(notice.waitForAbsence(timeout: 10))
        if UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone {
            // INF-2553, the captain's pick for an iPhone on its side, where the pill has no room: the words stay on
            // the place's own line until its next change, so they are never cleared unseen. In a stack of two, the
            // card that came back keeps them while the other card is up.
            let asked = try await home("asked-card")
            let second = try XCTUnwrap(asked["title"] as? String)
            showCard(second)
            turnPhone(to: .landscapeLeft, in: app, moving: cardHeading(second))
            _ = try await home("refuse-next-change", body: #"{"channel":"inf:cards:close","words":"\#(refusal)"}"#)
            tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
            showCard(note)
            XCTAssertFalse(app.staticTexts["card-error"].exists, "The words stay with the card that came back")
            showCard(second)
            let line = app.staticTexts["card-error"]
            XCTAssertTrue(line.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
            XCTAssertEqual(line.label, refusal)
            XCTAssertFalse(notice.exists, "On its side the words are on the card's line, not in a pill")
            picture("card-close-refused-on-its-side")
            // A message the computer refuses goes back in the box and says why on the composer's own line.
            let messageRefusal = "Your computer could not take this message. Try again."
            _ = try await home("refuse-next-change", body: #"{"channel":"inf:converse","words":"\#(messageRefusal)"}"#)
            let input = app.textFields["message-box"]
            let message = "Count the north buoys"
            focusForPhoneTyping(input, in: app); input.typeText(message)
            tapOnPhone(app.buttons["send-message"])
            let messageLine = app.staticTexts["message-problem"]
            XCTAssertTrue(messageLine.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
            XCTAssertEqual(messageLine.label, messageRefusal)
            XCTAssertEqual(input.value as? String, message, "A refused message goes back in the box")
            XCTAssertFalse(notice.exists, "On its side the words are on the composer's line, not in a pill")
            picture("message-refused-on-its-side")
            turnPhone(to: .portrait, in: app, moving: cardHeading(second))
            // Upright, the pill may still show the words until they leave on their own, and the lines stay quiet.
            XCTAssertTrue(notice.waitForAbsence(timeout: 20))
            XCTAssertFalse(messageLine.exists, "Upright, the pill says it instead of the composer's line")
            // The words go back out of the box, so the rest of the journey starts from an empty one.
            focusForPhoneTyping(input, in: app)
            input.typeText(String(repeating: XCUIKeyboardKey.delete.rawValue, count: message.count))
            let done = app.navigationBars.buttons["dismiss-phone-keyboard"]
            XCTAssertTrue(done.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription); tapOnPhone(done)
            XCTAssertTrue(app.keyboards.firstMatch.waitForAbsence(timeout: 10))
            tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
            XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(second).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
            showCard(note)
        }
        // INF-2794: the note's own Got it sits in the pinned row under the hairline and reads it; a press the
        // computer still holds has already taken the card off Home.
        let gotIt = app.buttons["note-done"]
        XCTAssertTrue(gotIt.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertEqual(gotIt.label, "Got it")
        picture("note-got-it")
        _ = try await home("hold-card-action", body: #"{"channel":"inf:cards:note-done"}"#)
        tapOnPhone(gotIt)
        _ = try await home("card-action-held")
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(note).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), "Got it shows at the tap, before the computer answers")
        _ = try await home("release-card-action")
        let closed = try await home("card-state", method: "GET")
        XCTAssertNotNil(closed["note"] as? [String: Any])
        XCTAssertEqual(closed["leaks"] as? Int, 0)
        // INF-1060, the captain: "after cards are dismissed, it doesn't extend back". With the last card closed,
        // the message box keeps its place and the column's width at the foot of Home.
        verifyPhoneComposerBounds(app: app)
        picture("cards-answered-and-closed")
        // INF-1059, the captain's "why images couldn't render inline?": a picture card already in the stack when the
        // phone comes back is drawn from the first cards read while the board read is still out, so its picture is asked
        // before the computer is in reach. The phone asks for it once it is in reach, rather than keeping a broken box.
        _ = try await home("offline")
        outOfReach()
        let late = try await home("late-picture-card")
        let lateTitle = try XCTUnwrap(late["title"] as? String)
        _ = try await home("online")
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(lateTitle).waitForPresence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.webViews.staticTexts[try XCTUnwrap(late["words"] as? String)].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        _ = try await home("board-read-held")
        _ = try await home("release-board-read")
        reach("In reach", timeout: 20)
        _ = try await home("late-picture-asked")
        picture("card-picture-after-reaching")
        tapOnPhone(app.buttons["put-aside-card"])
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(lateTitle).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10))
        // The same after view in both themes supplies the release note's native hero pair.
        let hero = try await home("hero-card")
        showCard(try XCTUnwrap(hero["title"] as? String))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.webViews.staticTexts["Chart for daylight sailing"].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        verifyPhoneComposerBounds(app: app)
        picture("cards-hero-light")
        _ = try await home("appearance-dark", budget: displayBudget)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.webViews.staticTexts["Chart for night sailing"].waitForPresence(timeout: 10))
        verifyPhoneComposerBounds(app: app)
        picture("cards-hero-dark")
        _ = try await home("appearance-light", budget: displayBudget)
        // INF-944 item 5 with INF-945's pick: the Mac's row, pinned at the card's foot with no scrolling,
        // the default last at the right and every choice keeping a 44-point touch area.
        let keepChoice = app.buttons["card-action-keep"], waitChoice = app.buttons["card-action-wait"]
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePress(keepChoice), "The choices sit in view without scrolling")
        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePress(waitChoice))
        // The answered count starts the first line, so the row wraps where its choices do not fit beside it.
        if abs(keepChoice.frame.midY - waitChoice.frame.midY) < 1 {
            XCTAssertLessThan(waitChoice.frame.maxX, keepChoice.frame.minX, "The default is drawn last")
        } else {
            XCTAssertGreaterThan(keepChoice.frame.minY, waitChoice.frame.minY, "The default is drawn last")
            XCTAssertEqual(keepChoice.frame.maxX, waitChoice.frame.maxX, accuracy: 1, "Each line sits at the trailing edge")
        }
        // XCUI reports the 44-point area in fractions of a pixel, such as 43.99999999999994.
        XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(keepChoice.frame.height.rounded(), 44)
        XCTAssertLessThan(keepChoice.frame.width, app.scrollViews["card-scroll"].frame.width / 2, "A choice keeps its own width")
        // INF-944 item 3: a card minimized on the computer leaves the phone's stack.
        // INF-1517, the captain's picks: Home keeps no Minimized menu; the card waits in Tasks under Waiting on you,
        // in its own row since it has no task, and a tap brings it back on Home and on the computer.
        let heroTitle = try XCTUnwrap(hero["title"] as? String)
        _ = try await home("minimize-hero")
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(heroTitle).waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        let pager = app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "card-pager").firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(pager.waitForAbsence(timeout: 10), "Home shows no Minimized menu")
        tab("Tasks")
        let restore = app.buttons.matching(identifier: "minimized-card").matching(NSPredicate(format: "label == %@", heroTitle)).firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(restore.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
        // INF-2928 piece 1: Waiting on you always shows its rows, so its header is a label, not a button, as on the Mac.
        XCTAssertLessThan(app.staticTexts["group-waiting"].frame.minY, restore.frame.minY, "It is listed under Waiting on you")
        picture("tasks-minimized")
        if UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone {
            // INF-2553: on an iPhone on its side, a bring-back the computer refuses puts the card aside again and says
            // why on the Tasks list's own line, as a refused bring-back did before.
            turnPhone(to: .landscapeLeft, in: app, moving: restore)
            _ = try await home("refuse-next-change", body: #"{"channel":"inf:cards:minimize","words":"\#(refusal)"}"#)
            tapOnPhone(restore)
            tab("Tasks")
            let asideLine = app.staticTexts["tasks-problem"]
            XCTAssertTrue(asideLine.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
            XCTAssertEqual(asideLine.label, refusal)
            XCTAssertTrue(restore.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), "A refused bring-back puts the card aside again")
            XCTAssertFalse(app.buttons["change-notice"].exists, "On its side the words are on the list's line, not in a pill")
            picture("bring-back-refused-on-its-side")
            turnPhone(to: .portrait, in: app, moving: restore)
            XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["change-notice"].waitForAbsence(timeout: 20))
        }
        tapOnPhone(restore)
        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(heroTitle).waitForPresence(timeout: 10), "Its row brings the card back on Home")
        XCTAssertEqual(waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate(format: "selected == true"), object: app.buttons["tab-home"], timeout: 10), .completed)
        let restored = try await home("hero-state", method: "GET")
        let restoredCard = try XCTUnwrap(restored["card"] as? [String: Any])
        XCTAssertNil(restoredCard["minimized"], "The phone brings it back on the computer too")
        // INF-209: the native frame remains usable at the largest standard Dynamic Type size.
        app.terminate()
        app.launchArguments += ["-UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName", "UICTContentSizeCategoryXXXL"]
        try await launchPhoneApp(app)
        reach("In reach", timeout: 20)
        showCard(try XCTUnwrap(hero["title"] as? String))
        let largeChoice = app.buttons["card-action-keep"]
        reveal(largeChoice)
        XCTAssertEqual(largeChoice.label, "Use this entrance")
        picture("card-large-type")
    }
}

+import Foundation
+import Security
+import XCTest
+@testable import InfinitaryKit
+
+/// INF-1109's review of the phone's approval key, repaired by INF-1250, on the disposable simulator's own
+/// Keychain: a new key replaces the kept record in place, under the same device name, and the phone reads it back.
+final class ApprovalKeyTests: XCTestCase {
+    /// Where the cleanup believes it runs. It can only narrow what the build allows, never widen it.
+    private var platform = ApprovalKey.Platform.current
+
+    override func setUpWithError() throws {
+        #if targetEnvironment(simulator)
+        forget()
+        #else
+        throw PhoneError.refused("Approval key tests require a disposable simulator.")
+        #endif
+    }
+
+    override func tearDownWithError() throws { forget() }
+
+    /// XCTest still calls teardown after setup throws, so the cleanup checks the build itself: outside the
+    /// disposable simulator the approval record is the person's own, and nothing is deleted.
+    private func forget() {
+        #if targetEnvironment(simulator)
+        guard platform == .simulator else { return }
+        let status = SecItemDelete([kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrService as String: ApprovalKey.service,
+            kSecAttrAccount as String: ApprovalKey.account, kSecAttrSynchronizable as String: false] as CFDictionary)
+        XCTAssertTrue(status == errSecSuccess || status == errSecItemNotFound, "\(status)")
+        #endif
+    }
+
+    func testReplacingTheKeyKeepsItsDeviceAndReadsTheNewKey() throws {
+        XCTAssertNil(try ApprovalKey.load())
+        let first = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), first)
+        let second = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        XCTAssertEqual(second.device, first.device)
+        XCTAssertNotEqual(second.publicKey, first.publicKey)
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), second)
+    }
+
+    /// The captain's ask on INF-1250's test: teardown on a physical iPhone or iPad leaves its approval record alone.
+    func testTeardownDeletesNothingOutsideTheSimulator() throws {
+        let kept = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        platform = .device
+        defer { platform = .current }
+        try tearDownWithError()
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), kept)
+    }
+
+    // INF-1109's unsigned device-test build must compile without the simulator-only damage helper.
+    // Keep this test and its record reader under the helper's own compilation boundary.
+    #if os(iOS) && targetEnvironment(simulator)
+    /// INF-1109's decision on a damaged record, on the disposable simulator's own Keychain: the phone check's
+    /// damaged record is refused by load and create alike and stays as it is, and only its own replacement
+    /// writes a new key, under a new device name. A device that cannot keep a key leaves it too.
+    func testADamagedRecordIsReplacedOnlyByItsOwnRepair() throws {
+        let kept = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        let original = try XCTUnwrap(record())
+        ApprovalKey.damageForPhoneCheck()
+        let damaged = try XCTUnwrap(record())
+        // The simulator branch must still exercise the actual destructive fixture, not merely compile it.
+        XCTAssertFalse(damaged.isEmpty)
+        XCTAssertLessThan(damaged.count, original.count)
+        XCTAssertEqual(damaged, original.prefix(damaged.count))
+        var damage: ApprovalKey.Damage?
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.load()) { error in
+            if case PhoneError.damagedApproval(let found) = error { damage = found }
+        }
+        XCTAssertEqual(damage, ApprovalKey.Damage(damaged))
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.create())
+        XCTAssertEqual(record(), damaged)
+        let found = try XCTUnwrap(damage)
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.replace(found, on: .device, in: DeviceKeychain()))
+        XCTAssertEqual(record(), damaged)
+
+        let fresh = try ApprovalKey.replace(found)
+        XCTAssertNotEqual(fresh.device, kept.device)
+        XCTAssertNotEqual(fresh.publicKey, kept.publicKey)
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), fresh)
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.replace(found), "The damaged record is gone, so the same choice replaces nothing")
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), fresh)
+    }
+
+    /// The approval record's bytes as the simulator's Keychain keeps them.
+    private func record() -> Data? {
+        var item: CFTypeRef?
+        let status = SecItemCopyMatching([kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrService as String: ApprovalKey.service,
+            kSecAttrAccount as String: ApprovalKey.account, kSecAttrSynchronizable as String: false,
+            kSecReturnData as String: true] as CFDictionary, &item)
+        return status == errSecSuccess ? item as? Data : nil
+    }
+    #endif
+}

+import XCTest
+
+/// The cards-place part (scripts/phone-test-plan.ts): its test and the steps only it takes.
+extension PhoneJourney {
+    /// INF-3124, the captain: "interacting with a thread on a card: currently, it auto scroll down to the latest message
+    /// update at the bottom. That disrupts my flow", with direction B and the jump down whenever they read above.
+    /// Data: a first mate card whose fourteen-message thread is longer than its back on the iPhone and the iPad, then two new first mate lines.
+    /// Completion: the back opens at its foot with no jump down; scrolled to its start it shows a plain arrow; the two
+    /// new lines leave the first message where it was and count "↓ 2 new"; the jump goes to the first of them; then, at
+    /// its foot, two exchanges of a reply and the stand-in first mate's answer each stay in view with no jump down.
+    func testThreadKeepsItsPlace() async throws {
+        try await launchJoined()
+        let fixture = try await home("place-card")
+        let title = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["title"] as? String)
+        let first = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["first"] as? String)
+        let count = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["count"] as? Int)
+        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(title).waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
+        waitForShownBodyRevealed()
+        let cue = app.buttons["thread-cue"]
+        XCTAssertTrue(cue.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
+        reveal(cue); tapOnPhone(cue)
+        let back = app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "card-back").firstMatch
+        XCTAssertTrue(back.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
+        let thread = app.scrollViews["card-thread"]
+        let jump = app.buttons["thread-jump"]
+        let opening = back.staticTexts[first]
+        // A thread opens at its foot, where nothing waits below.
+        waitForSteadyTarget(thread)
+        XCTAssertFalse(jump.exists, "The thread opened above its foot\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+        // The captain scrolls back to the thread's start; the jump down shows as a plain arrow.
+        for _ in 0..<8 where !(opening.exists && opening.isHittable) { thread.swipeDown() }
+        waitForSteadyTarget(opening)
+        XCTAssertTrue(opening.isHittable, "The thread's first message cannot be reached\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+        XCTAssertTrue(jump.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
+        XCTAssertEqual(jump.label, "↓")
+        let before = opening.frame
+        picture("1-thread-read-from-its-start")
+        let more = try await home("place-card-more")
+        let added = try XCTUnwrap(more["added"] as? String)
+        let label = app.staticTexts["thread-count"]
+        let arrived = NSPredicate { _, _ in label.exists && label.label == "THREAD · \(count + 2)" }
+        XCTAssertEqual(waitForPhonePredicate(arrived, object: nil, timeout: 20), .completed, app.debugDescription)
+        // The new lines move nothing: the first message holds its place, and the jump counts them.
+        let counted = NSPredicate { _, _ in jump.exists && jump.label == "↓ 2 NEW" }
+        XCTAssertEqual(waitForPhonePredicate(counted, object: nil, timeout: 10), .completed, app.debugDescription)
+        waitForSteadyTarget(opening)
+        XCTAssertEqual(opening.frame.minY, before.minY, accuracy: 1, "A new line moved the thread\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+        picture("2-two-new-below")
+        // The jump goes to the first new line.
+        tapOnPhone(jump)
+        let firstNew = back.staticTexts[added]
+        XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePress(firstNew), "The jump did not reach the first new line\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+        picture("3-at-the-new-lines")
+        // At its foot the thread follows: across two exchanges the captain's reply and the answer are in view, and no jump
+        // down shows.
+        let answer = try XCTUnwrap(fixture["replyAnswer"] as? String)
+        let reply = app.textFields["card-reply"]
+        let send = app.buttons["send-reply"]
+        for exchange in 1...2 {
+            XCTAssertFalse(jump.exists, "The thread left its foot before exchange \(exchange)\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+            let words = "Exchange \(exchange): go ahead with Thursday."
+            reveal(reply); focusForPhoneTyping(reply, in: app); reply.typeText(words)
+            reveal(send); tapOnPhone(send)
+            // A line just added reads no tap point while the thread scrolls it into view, so each line is first read inside
+            // the thread's frame, then as pressable.
+            let sent = back.staticTexts[words]
+            XCTAssertTrue(waitForInThread(sent, thread), "The reply is not in view\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+            XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePress(sent), "The reply is not in view\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+            let answers = back.staticTexts.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label == %@", answer))
+            let answered = NSPredicate { _, _ in answers.count == exchange }
+            XCTAssertEqual(waitForPhonePredicate(answered, object: nil, timeout: 30), .completed, app.debugDescription)
+            let latest = answers.element(boundBy: exchange - 1)
+            XCTAssertTrue(waitForInThread(latest, thread), "Answer \(exchange) is not in view\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+            XCTAssertTrue(waitForPhonePress(latest), "Answer \(exchange) is not in view\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+            XCTAssertFalse(jump.exists, "Answer \(exchange) was counted, not shown\n\(app.debugDescription)")
+        }
+        picture("4-following-at-the-foot")
+    }
+
+    /// Whether `line` comes to sit wholly inside the thread's own frame, read from frames alone.
+    private func waitForInThread(_ line: XCUIElement, _ thread: XCUIElement) -> Bool {
+        let inside = NSPredicate { _, _ in
+            line.exists && !line.frame.isEmpty && thread.frame.contains(line.frame)
+        }
+        return waitForPhonePredicate(inside, object: nil, timeout: 10) == .completed
+    }
+}

+
+        // The card's face: the button at one line and at two, a pull from the head, a tap on the head.

+        focusForPhoneTyping(reply, in: app)

+        hideButtonBesideSend("face, two lines", send: app.buttons["send-reply"], into: &failures)
+        picture("2-face-reply-two-lines")

+        XCTAssertTrue(hide.waitForAbsence(timeout: 5), "The keyboard-down button stays with the keyboard down")
+        focusForPhoneTyping(reply, in: app)

+import Foundation

+@testable import InfinitaryKit

+/// INF-1109's review of the phone's approval key, repaired by INF-1250, on the disposable simulator's own
+/// Keychain: a new key replaces the kept record in place, under the same device name, and the phone reads it back.
+final class ApprovalKeyTests: XCTestCase {
+    /// Where the cleanup believes it runs. It can only narrow what the build allows, never widen it.
+    private var platform = ApprovalKey.Platform.current
+
+    override func setUpWithError() throws {
+        #if targetEnvironment(simulator)
+        forget()
+        #else
+        throw PhoneError.refused("Approval key tests require a disposable simulator.")
+        #endif
+    }
+
+    override func tearDownWithError() throws { forget() }
+
+    /// XCTest still calls teardown after setup throws, so the cleanup checks the build itself: outside the
+    /// disposable simulator the approval record is the person's own, and nothing is deleted.
+    private func forget() {
+        #if targetEnvironment(simulator)
+        guard platform == .simulator else { return }
+        let status = SecItemDelete([kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrService as String: ApprovalKey.service,
+            kSecAttrAccount as String: ApprovalKey.account, kSecAttrSynchronizable as String: false] as CFDictionary)
+        XCTAssertTrue(status == errSecSuccess || status == errSecItemNotFound, "\(status)")
+        #endif
+    }
+
+    func testReplacingTheKeyKeepsItsDeviceAndReadsTheNewKey() throws {
+        XCTAssertNil(try ApprovalKey.load())
+        let first = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), first)
+        let second = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        XCTAssertEqual(second.device, first.device)
+        XCTAssertNotEqual(second.publicKey, first.publicKey)
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), second)
+    }
+
+    /// The captain's ask on INF-1250's test: teardown on a physical iPhone or iPad leaves its approval record alone.
+    func testTeardownDeletesNothingOutsideTheSimulator() throws {
+        let kept = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        platform = .device
+        defer { platform = .current }
+        try tearDownWithError()
+        XCTAssertEqual(try ApprovalKey.load(), kept)
+    }
+
+    // INF-1109's unsigned device-test build must compile without the simulator-only damage helper.
+    // Keep this test and its record reader under the helper's own compilation boundary.
+    #if os(iOS) && targetEnvironment(simulator)
+    /// INF-1109's decision on a damaged record, on the disposable simulator's own Keychain: the phone check's
+    /// damaged record is refused by load and create alike and stays as it is, and only its own replacement
+    /// writes a new key, under a new device name. A device that cannot keep a key leaves it too.
+    func testADamagedRecordIsReplacedOnlyByItsOwnRepair() throws {
+        let kept = try ApprovalKey.create()
+        let original = try XCTUnwrap(record())
+        ApprovalKey.damageForPhoneCheck()
+        let damaged = try XCTUnwrap(record())
+        // The simulator branch must still exercise the actual destructive fixture, not merely compile it.
+        XCTAssertFalse(damaged.isEmpty)
+        XCTAssertLessThan(damaged.count, original.count)
+        XCTAssertEqual(damaged, original.prefix(damaged.count))

+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.load()) { error in

+        }

+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try ApprovalKey.create())

+            kSecAttrAccount as String: ApprovalKey.account, kSecAttrSynchronizable as String: false,
+            kSecReturnData as String: true] as CFDictionary, &item)
+        return status == errSecSuccess ? item as? Data : nil
+    }
+    #endif

+        // INF-1109: the shared body says confirmation comes before sharing without naming a device, and that
+        // temporary access is only the computer's; no Allow here offers it.
+        XCTAssertTrue(body("after you confirm").exists, app.debugDescription)
+        XCTAssertFalse(body("Your computer asks you to confirm").exists, app.debugDescription)
+        let temporary = body("Temporary access is available only on your computer")
+        XCTAssertTrue(temporary.exists, app.debugDescription)
+        // INF-1109: the foot names the requested secret by name, environment, reference and version, beside
+        // choices that stay in the card's frame rather than scrolling away with its body.
+        let named = app.staticTexts["approval-secret-calendar"]
+        XCTAssertTrue(named.waitForPresence(timeout: 10), app.debugDescription)
+        XCTAssertEqual(named.label, "Planning calendar (Personal, calendar, version 1)")
+        XCTAssertTrue(app.descendants(matching: .any)["card-frame"].exists, "The choices stay pinned: \(app.debugDescription)")
+        // The choices take a press once the computer's body is revealed at its drawn height, as every card's do.
+        waitUntilEnabled(allow)
+        XCTAssertTrue(allow.isHittable, app.debugDescription)
+        picture("secrets-use")
+        // The scope lies below an iPhone's fold; the body scrolls to it while the pinned choices stay.
+        let reading = app.scrollViews["card-scroll"]
+        revealPhoneCardReading(temporary, in: reading, app: app)
+        XCTAssertTrue(phoneCardReadingBounds(reading, app: app).contains(phoneAccessibilityBounds(temporary.frame)),
+            "The scope reads whole \(temporary.frame) inside \(phoneCardReadingBounds(reading, app: app))")
+        XCTAssertTrue(allow.isHittable, app.debugDescription)
+        picture("secrets-use-scope")
+        let waiting = try await home("secrets-state", method: "GET")
+        let asked = try XCTUnwrap(waiting["confirmed"] as? Int)
+        // perform() puts a failed approval in the card's error foot, not the body's informational notice.
+        let confirmationError = app.staticTexts["card-error"]
+        XCTAssertFalse(confirmationError.exists, app.debugDescription)
+        var confirmationProblem: String?
+        func confirmationRefused() -> Bool {
+            if confirmationProblem != nil { return true }
+            guard confirmationError.exists else { return false }
+            confirmationProblem = confirmationError.label
+            return true
+        }
+        func requireConfirmationNotRefused() async throws {
+            guard confirmationRefused() else { return }
+            picture("secrets-confirmation-refused")
+            let refused = try await home("secrets-state", method: "GET")
+            let pending = try XCTUnwrap((refused["uses"] as? [[String: Any]])?.first {
+                $0["request"] as? String == first["request"] as? String
+            })
+            XCTAssertEqual(pending["state"] as? String, "waiting", "A failed confirmation leaves the same use waiting")
+            XCTAssertEqual(refused["sent"] as? [Bool], [], "An unconfirmed Allow sends nothing")
+            XCTAssertEqual(refused["confirmed"] as? Int, asked, "A failed phone confirmation does not ask on the computer")
+            throw NSError(domain: "PhoneSecretsConfirmation", code: 1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey:
+                "The phone did not confirm the use: \(confirmationProblem ?? "No confirmation result")"])
+        }
+        reveal(allow); tapOnPhone(allow, repeatDiscarded: false)
+        // INF-1109: the system can fail to start Face ID. That is a terminal refusal, not an optional permission
+        // alert still to come. Observe the card's error too, keep the no-send proof, and never retry Allow.
+        let springboard = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "com.apple.springboard")
+        let permitted = springboard.alerts.buttons["OK"]
+        _ = waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in confirmationRefused() || permitted.exists }, object: nil, timeout: 10)
+        try await requireConfirmationNotRefused()
+        if permitted.exists { picture("secrets-face-id-permission"); tapOnPhone(permitted, repeatDiscarded: false) }
+        picture("secrets-face-id")
+        _ = try await home("face-in-view")
+        let confirmationEnded = waitForPhonePredicate(NSPredicate { _, _ in
+            confirmationRefused() || !self.cardHeading(title).exists
+        }, object: nil, timeout: 30)
+        // Stop the owned simulator's face before an assertion can end this test, including a late refusal.
+        _ = try await home("face-away")
+        try await requireConfirmationNotRefused()
+        guard confirmationEnded == .completed else {
+            throw NSError(domain: "PhoneSecretsConfirmation", code: 2, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey:
+                "The phone did not finish its confirmation: \(app.debugDescription)"])
+        }
+        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(title).waitForAbsence(timeout: 30), app.debugDescription)
+        picture("secrets-allowed")
+        var state = try await home("secrets-state", method: "GET")
+        let enrolled = try XCTUnwrap(devices.first?["device"] as? String)
+        let allowed = try XCTUnwrap((state["history"] as? [[String: Any]])?.first { $0["request"] as? String == first["request"] as? String })
+        XCTAssertEqual(allowed["state"] as? String, "completed")
+        XCTAssertEqual(allowed["approval"] as? String, "remote")
+        XCTAssertEqual(allowed["device"] as? String, enrolled)
+        XCTAssertEqual(state["sent"] as? [Bool], [true], "The calendar received the entry once")
+        XCTAssertEqual(state["confirmed"] as? Int, asked, "An Allow from this phone asks for no confirmation on the computer")
+
+        // Deny needs no Face ID and runs nothing.
+        let second = try await home("secrets-request")
+        showCard(title)
+        let deny = app.buttons["approval-deny"]
+        XCTAssertTrue(deny.waitForPresence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
+        // A press while the body still lays out could land beside a moving choice; it waits for the reveal gate.
+        waitUntilEnabled(deny)
+        reveal(deny); tapOnPhone(deny, repeatDiscarded: false)
+        XCTAssertTrue(cardHeading(title).waitForAbsence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
+        state = try await home("secrets-state", method: "GET")
+        let denied = try XCTUnwrap((state["history"] as? [[String: Any]])?.first { $0["request"] as? String == second["request"] as? String })
+        XCTAssertEqual(denied["state"] as? String, "denied")
+        XCTAssertEqual(state["sent"] as? [Bool], [true], "A refusal sends nothing")
+        XCTAssertEqual((state["cards"] as? [Any])?.count, 0)
+
+        // The phone's record is damaged by the next launch: Settings says so, and Set up approvals offers nothing.
+        app.launchEnvironment["INFINITARY_DAMAGED_APPROVAL"] = "1"
+        try await launchPhoneApp(app)
+        app.launchEnvironment.removeValue(forKey: "INFINITARY_DAMAGED_APPROVAL")
+        reach("In reach", timeout: 20)
+        openSettings()
+        let again = app.buttons["approval-set-up"]
+        XCTAssertTrue(again.waitForPresence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
+        // The same setup control must finish entering in its damaged-record state too; presence is not readiness.
+        waitForSteadyTarget(again)
+        picture("secrets-settings-damaged")
+        XCTAssertEqual(again.label, "Set up approvals again")
+        XCTAssertTrue(again.isHittable, "The choice shows at the sheet's medium height, with no scrolling")
+        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["approval-damaged"].exists, app.debugDescription)
+        XCTAssertFalse(app.staticTexts["approval-problem"].exists, "A damaged record does not ask to unlock the phone")
+        tapOnPhone(again, repeatDiscarded: false)
+        let replaced = app.staticTexts["approval-code"]
+        XCTAssertTrue(replaced.waitForPresence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
+        let newCode = replaced.label.replacingOccurrences(of: "Code ", with: "")
+        XCTAssertNotEqual(newCode, shown, "Set up approvals again offers a new key")
+        picture("secrets-settings-damaged-code")
+        closeSettings()
+
+        // Only the computer's own confirmation enrolls the new key, and the earlier enrollment stays there.
+        let reoffered = try await home("secrets-state", method: "GET")
+        XCTAssertEqual((reoffered["devices"] as? [[String: Any]])?.map { $0["device"] as? String }, [enrolled])
+        let reconfirmed = try await home("secrets-confirm")
+        XCTAssertEqual(reconfirmed["code"] as? String, newCode, "The computer's card shows the new code this phone shows")
+        XCTAssertEqual(reconfirmed["confirmed"] as? Int, 1)
+        let both = try XCTUnwrap(reconfirmed["devices"] as? [[String: Any]])
+        XCTAssertEqual(Set(both.compactMap { $0["code"] as? String }), [shown, newCode])
+        XCTAssertFalse(both.contains { $0["code"] as? String == newCode && $0["device"] as? String == enrolled },
+                       "The new key is enrolled under a new device name")
+        openSettings()
+        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["approval-enrolled"].waitForPresence(timeout: 20), app.debugDescription)
+        picture("secrets-settings-damaged-enrolled")
+        closeSettings()
+    }
+
